claude.sample_unit: individuals (men 74,880; women 80,133) aged 40-70 without prior CVD or diabetes

links.outcome: Calibration (observed/expected ratio) of SCORE2 by socioeconomic and ethnic subgroups
links.effect: Low-risk model underpredicted CVD overall (OE 1.30 men, 1.22 women), most in lowest SES (1.54 men, 1.64 women) and Surinamese subgroups (1.92 men, 1.86 women); lowest-SES Surinamese men OE 2.53.
links.quote: Underprediction in the Surinamese subgroup was largest (OE-ratio 1.9, in men and women), particularly in the low socioeconomic Surinamese subgroups (OE-ratio 2.5 and 2.1 in men and women).

links.outcome: Local performance of SCORE2 low-risk model in Dutch routine care population versus development
links.effect: 6966 CVD events observed versus 5495 predicted by the low-risk model intended for the Netherlands; OE-ratio 1.30 men and 1.22 women; C-statistics 0.70 and 0.72.
links.quote: At external validation of the SCORE2 low-risk model (intended for use in the Netherlands), we found that for the total population the SCORE2 low-risk model predicted 5495 CVD events in the population included in this study, whereas 6966 CVD events were observed.

links.outcome: Whether switching to higher-risk SCORE2 recalibrated models improved calibration in underpredicted subgroups
links.effect: In subgroups with underprediction, moderate/high-risk models improved OE-ratios (e.g., moderate-risk OE 1.02 overall; high-risk OE 1.05 in other-ethnicity men), though Surinamese men remained at 1.45.
links.quote: In the subgroups with underprediction in the low-risk model, the intermediate or high-risk SCORE2 models showed improved OE-ratios.

links.outcome: Subgroup calibration and discrimination of SCORE2 by SES and ethnicity
links.effect: Underprediction was larger in low SES (OE 1.5 men, 1.6 women) and Surinamese subgroups (OE up to 2.5); discrimination moderate, C-statistics 0.63 to 0.76 across subgroups.
links.quote: Underprediction was larger in low socioeconomic subgroups of the overall study population (OE-ratio 1.5 and 1.6 in men and women, respectively), and comparable in Dutch and the combined "other ethnicities" low socioeconomic subgroups.

links.outcome: Underprediction where model omits socioeconomic status and ethnicity as inputs
links.effect: Model excluding SES and ethnicity underpredicted risk in low-SES and Surinamese subgroups; authors recommend including these as predictors or adjusting risk within countries.
links.quote: Including socioeconomic status and ethnicity as predictors in CVD risk models and implementing CVD risk adjustment within countries is desirable for adequate CVD risk prediction and counselling.

links.outcome: Performance of SCORE2 varying across regional models and subgroups
links.effect: Performance differed by risk-model calibration and subgroup; low-risk model underpredicted, high and very-high models overpredicted in the total population.
links.quote: The high-risk model and very-high-risk model (intended for use in Eastern Europe) showed overprediction in men and women for the total population, with an OE-ratio below 1 ( Fig. 1 ).

unlisted_practices: Recalibrating or selecting a higher-risk regional model version for high-risk subgroups within a country

links.effect: OE-ratio was 1.30 (95% CI 1.30–1.30) in men and 1.22 (95% CI 1.21–1.22) in women.
links.quote: Calibration showed an OE-ratio (observed/mean expected ratio) of 1.30 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.30–1.30) in men and 1.22 (95% CI 1.21–1.22) in women ( Fig. 1 ).

links.effect: Low socioeconomic subgroups had OE-ratio 1.5 in men and 1.6 in women.

links.effect: Surinamese OE-ratio was 1.9 in men and women; low socioeconomic Surinamese OE-ratio 2.5 in men and 2.1 in women.
links.quote: Underprediction in the Surinamese subgroup was largest (OE-ratio 1.9, in men and women), particularly in the low socioeconomic Surinamese subgroups (OE-ratio 2.5 and 2.1 in men and women).

links.effect: Predicted 5,495 CVD events versus 6,966 observed; OE-ratio 1.30 (95% CI 1.30-1.30) in men and 1.22 (95% CI 1.21-1.22) in women
links.quote: At external validation of the SCORE2 low-risk model (intended for use in the Netherlands), we found that for the total population the SCORE2 low-risk model predicted 5495 CVD events in the population included in this study, whereas 6966 CVD events were observed.

links.outcome: CVD risk calibration across socioeconomic and ethnic subgroups
links.effect: OE-ratio in low-risk model ranged from 1.54 to 1.17 across SES in men, 1.64 to 0.94 in women, and was 1.92 in Surinamese men and 1.86 in Surinamese women
links.quote: However, in terms of calibration the performance of the SCORE2 low-risk model was particularly poor in low socioeconomic subgroups and in Surinamese subgroups.

links.quote: In general, at calibration in socioeconomic subgroups for the total population the SCORE2 models showed more extreme underprediction in subgroups at lower socioeconomic status.
